issues.detail: The Hebrew 'מְגוּרֵי אֶל חֶרֶב' means 'those who are terrified of the sword' or 'those who flee to the sword' (from the root גור, 'to sojourn/dread'), not 'those living at Ê-léc' (a place name). The Vietnamese renders 'Ê-léc' as a location, which is a misreading of the Hebrew word 'אֶל' (to/toward) plus 'חֶרֶב' (sword), and adds a place name not present in the text.
